category: remote file conveyor (posting workstation) with a resold premium-download pool
tier: daily disk plan + premium traffic + converter hours

free_tier.stated: No free tier. 'There is no free trial, but any plan can be paid for 10, 20 or 30 days.' The smallest published plan is 20 GB for 10 days at $5.20.
free_tier.notes: Three independent billing streams: disk plan, premium traffic, converter hours.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the service downloads into a disk plan, it does not publish a maximum object size
per_object_cap.notes: The disk plan is the ceiling: 20 GB to 2 TB, chosen per day.

retention.stated: For the length of the paid plan; the plan can be changed once a day. No post-expiry retention statement found on the pricing page.

egress.terms: 'Unlimited traffic' on every disk plan. Downloads that need a premium file-host account are bought separately: '$0.36 per 10 GB ... billed strictly by bytes actually downloaded.'
egress.free_allowance: unlimited disk-plan traffic; no included premium-pool allowance
egress.price_per_tb: USD 0.36 per 10 GB of premium-pool download (USD 36.86 per TiB)

interface_detail: Browser cockpit at coolspeeds.com/{en,ru}/cabinet.html; ruTorrent 3.x with 19 plugins for torrents; FTP for uploads; a Firefox extension (LeechGrab) routes browser downloads through the vendor's MITM proxy. No public API documented on the pages read.
tooling: Web UI only as documented; purchase links are plain cabinet URLs (action=s40&days=30), so a plan can be bought by URL. Torrents are handled by the vendor's ruTorrent instance, not by a local client.
chaining: It replaces a seedbox plus a VPS for the posting workflow: download from a host, repack, upload to 100+ hosts, emit a post. As a pure debrid it is the premium-traffic stream at $0.036/GB.

limits.value: download up to 10 Gbit/s, seed up to 16 Mbit/s
premium-pool downloads are prepaid in 10 GB packs; no included allowance
converter billed per actual CPU minute with a user-chosen priority multiplier; higher multiplier costs more

limits_note: The FAQ says premium traffic is only needed 'when a file host requires a premium account and you do not have one'; your own host accounts can be plugged in instead.
binding_note: At 1 TiB a month the disk plan is irrelevant (100 GB is $34.80/month) but the premium pool is $36.86 per TiB, prepaid in 10 GB steps, and every byte is billed. That purchase, not a rate limit, is what the client meets first. The old documentation page still states '$0.30 per GB'; the live pricing page says $0.36 per 10 GB, and this record keeps the live number.

identity_cost.detail: An account in the cabinet is required to hold a plan and a traffic balance. The signup form itself was not read; email is the minimum such a cabinet implies and is not confirmed.

reliability_note: Payment is crypto and WebMoney only, so a plan cannot be bought with a card; the operator has run since 2011 and bills per byte, but the premium pool is a shared resale pool and the documentation already warns that 'bezotkaznaya rabota ... dlya vsekh failoobmennikov ne garantiruetsya' (uninterrupted operation for all file hosts is not guaranteed).
confidence_note: Prices, plan sizes and the payment-method list are quoted from the live English and Russian pricing pages read today. A test download through the premium pool would raise this to measured.

evidence.proved: plan sizes and prices (40 GB for 30 days $20.40; 100 GB for 30 days $34.80; 1025 GB for 30 days $36.00), 'Unlimited traffic', '$0.36 per 10 GB', 'seed up to 16 Mbit/s', and the payment list 'Bitcoin, Litecoin, USDT (7 networks ...), WebMoney'
'19 тарифов по объёму диска и 2 фиксированных месячных. Трафик безлимитный. Тариф можно менять раз в сутки.' and the per-plan dollar prices in the Russian interface

the premium traffic is bought from external link-unrestricting services, the price there is '0.30$ za GB' (an older figure than the live page), and 'bezotkaznaya rabota dannoy funktsii dlya vsekh failoobmennikov ne garantiruetsya'
the service downloads either through the client's own premium host accounts or through 'premium traffic' bought from external link-unrestricting services

price_per_tb_month: USD 36.86 per TiB of premium-pool download, plus USD 34.80/month for the 100 GB disk plan
notes: The cheapest per-GB figure found. The caveat is payment: crypto or WebMoney only, so a client without either cannot buy it at all. Candidate explanations considered for the price gap between the docs page ($0.30/GB) and the live page ($0.36/10 GB): (1) the docs page is a 2021 capture never updated - supported by its image timestamps uploads/images/gallery/2021-02 and by the pricing page being the later artefact; (2) the two pages price different pools; no evidence. The record keeps the live pricing page.
